TextEng: A talking chicken arrived at my stronghold and begged (clucked?) for my help. This strange bird claims that she is really a druid named Jaeda who was afflicted by an evil polymorph curse. She asked me to take her to the Brush of Barbs and find the twin oaks where her leader, a druid named Tatham, is imprisoned. At the twin oaks, I should speak the magical passwords: Cloudberry and Bilberry. I hope that this strange tale proves true, and that I have not embarked on a wild chicken chase.

At Govan's Grove in the Brush of Barbs, a talking seagull named Tatham has told me that his circle of druids was attacked by a rebel druid named Stegil. Tatham and his fellow druids were cursed and polymorphed into helpless fowls. I have already found Jaeda (the chicken), and Tatham (the seagull); however, two druids are still missing (Wanix and Urith). I must search for one druid in Gillian's Hill and for the other druid in Liam's Hold. After finding each druid, I should return them to Govan's Grove in the Brush of Barbs.

In Gillian's Hill, I found the druid named Urith, who was polymorphed into a penguin. Now I must seek the druid named Wanix in Liam's Hold. After finding Wanix, I should return him to Govan's Grove in the Brush of Barbs. There, among the ancient stones, the seagull named Tatham will have further instructions.

In Liam's Hold, I found the druid named Wanix, who was polymorphed into a parrot. Now I must seek the druid named Urith in Gillian's Hill. After finding Urith, I should return her to Govan's Grove in the Brush of Barbs. There, among the ancient stones, the seagull named Tatham will have further instructions.

I have found all of the missing druids: Jaeda the chicken, Tatham the seagull, Urith the penguin, and Wanix the parrot. Tatham, the leader of this motley flock, has asked me to find Stegil's magical bloodstone, which can be used to break the foul fowl curse which afflicts the four druids. Tatham suggested that I begin my search at the Tree of Blood located deep in the Wild Hills. Once I have the bloodstone, I must return to the Brush of Barbs and seek Tatham's council.

In Stegil's burrow, I rescued a young half-elf named Feynemonee. She betrayed Tatham and the other druids by helping Stegil, but she also expressed remorse for her actions. Hoping to find peace with nature, she told me to search for Stegil's magical bloodstone hidden behind a loose stone in the burrow's wall. I should begin my search beneath the stuffed elk's head mounted on the wall. After finding the bloodstone, I must return to the Brush of Barbs and seek Tatham's council.

I have made a dark pact with the rebel druid Stegil. To fulfill this pact, I must return to the Bush of Barbs and betray the four fowl druids. After killing the birds, I must bring their hearts to Stegil's burrow as sacrifices to the god of beasts, Malar. I can only suppose that Malar is not terribly fond of birds.

I have fulfilled my dark pact with the rebel druid Stegil. I have slain the four fowl druids and have given their hearts to Stegil who devoured them in Malar's name. As a reward for my betrayal, Stegil now offers me the blessing of Malar and other druidic services.

Using the bloodstone which I recovered from Stegil, the four unfortunate druids reversed the polymorph curse and returned to their normal forms. As a reward for my assistance, Tatham now offers me healing and other druidic services.

A talking chicken arrived at my stronghold asking for my help. She was pursued by a hungry butcher, and I let the butcher have the chicken for his stew-pot. I shall always wonder why that little chicken wanted my help.
A Circle of Fowl

After downing some of the dread Kneecracker Cider in the Happy Cow Tavern, Fulbar told me a rumor about a grain shortage in Daggerford. He recommended I check in with Maerovyna, the priestess of Chauntea, who resides in the Harvest House.

Maerovyna is concerned about these rumors of a grain shortage and asks that I check in with Daggerford's chief grain provider, a sanguine fellow named Fernd, who runs the grist-mill in the farmlands east of Daggerford.
After uncovering Loru's true identity, I slew the dread slaad, ending its evil designs for Fernd and his fellow farmers.

I've encountered the miller, Fernd, and am saddened by the man's unenviable state. Apparently, his grief over losing his love to another has progressed to full-blown psychosis, where he blathers on about "secrets" and "flour" in a nonsensical fashion. I must find some way to alleviate the fellow's pain, before he reaches a state of madness from which he can never return.

A rather calm and pious monk named Loru is living in a small cave adjacent to the basement beneath Fernd's gristmill. It seems an odd place for a holy man to reside, but he seems genuinely concerned over the miller's agitated state.

I found the journal of Loru the slaad, currently disguised as Loru the monk. Apparently, he's using the miller, Fernd, as a tool in some grand scheme designed to bring slaadi into our world from the chaotic plane called Limbo.

After uncovering Loru's true identity, I slew the dread slaad, ending its evil designs for Fernd and his fellow farmers. Now, I should visit Maerovyna at Chauntea's Shrine in Daggerford, to tell her of my discovery.

Maerovyna was impressed by my ability to thwart the plans of the evil slaad, Loru. She says she will dispatch an acolyte to Fernd's mill to help expedite the man's recovery. Grain production should soon return to normal levels.

Maerovyna was disappointed that my resolution to solving the miller's issues had been to kill the miller. She says she will dispatch an acolyte to Fernd's mill to oversee the man's burial, and the resumption of grain production.
After uncovering Loru's true identity, I slew the dread slaad, ending its evil designs for Fernd and his fellow farmers.

After uncovering Loru's true identity, I slew the dread slaad, ending its designs for Fernd and his fellow farmers. If Maerovyna was still alive I'm sure she'd be pleased with the outcome, but better to have served the Lord of Murder than some nature goddess!
A Mad Miller

Deep beneath my stronghold, I discovered a ruined temple dedicated to Bhaal, Lord of Murder. Xatuum, the resident high priest, lost contact with Bhaal decades ago but continues to pray each day, faithfully awaiting a response from his god. Over time, Xatuum's flesh rotted and decayed, but his life is still sustained by his undying faith in Bhaal. Xatuum believes that the ritual sacrifice of ten pureblooded men or women will attract Bhaal's attention. To this end, Xatuum has asked me to collect the heart blood of ten humanoids: dwarves, elves, humans, halflings, or gnomes. To collect the blood, the high priest gave me a magic bag, which contains ten special vials. Once I have collected ten vials of blood, I should return to Xatuum.
I have collected the ten vials of blood requested by Xatuum, the undead high priest who inhabits the lower level of my stronghold. I should return to Xatuum and see if his ritual can awaken Bhaal.

Deep beneath my stronghold, I discovered a ruined temple dedicated to Bhaal, Lord of Murder. Xatuum, the resident high priest, lost contact with Bhaal decades ago but continued to pray each day, faithfully awaiting a response from his god. Xatuum performed an arcane ritual using the blood sacrifices that I dutifully collected, but even this ritual failed to attract Bhaal's notice. In a fit of rage, Xatuum turned against me and I was forced to slay him. Somehow, I doubt that even in death Xatuum will be finding much peace.
Bhaal's Bag of Blood
While traveling through the farmlands west of Daggerford, I came upon a friendly farmer and his teenage son who invited me to sit down with them for a cupful of hot apple cider. Sounds tasty!
I decided to take Jonas Senior and his son up on their offer to sit down with them for hot apple cider. As an added benefit, I'll also be on hand for the boy's birthday party.
I couldn't help feeling uneasy when entering the Maxillian's country estate. My "sixth sense" was accurate, it seems, as the friendly farmers turned out to be hungry werewolves!

I've become an unwilling participant in a game Jonas Senior calls "Only the Strongest Survive." Having been drugged, I have now awoken in a small cell with no possessions other than some drab prison garb.
Jonas Senior has released me into the Chase Maze, where I must try to escape before he counts down to zero. If I fail, I shall come face-to-face with his very hungry son.
I have escaped the dread Chase Maze. Perhaps the matriarch of this disturbed family can shed some light on events here, and help me locate my stolen belongings!

I conversed with Gravia Maxillian, who asked that I return to the maze and ensure that neither her son nor husband survive. I've heard of family members at each other's throats, but this is ridiculous!
Gravia was grateful to hear I'd slain the two werewolves who have been terrorizing the Trade Way. Perhaps the line of Maxillian werewolves will be severed at last.
I have slain the entire family of lycanthropes who have been terrorizing the Trade Way. Perhaps the line of Maxillian werewolves will be severed at last.
Birthday Present

Captain Frederick, of the Daggerford Militia, has asked me to look in on some wild elves who are causing problems for the local farmers. He said I should speak with their leader, Kyleena Moonglow, whose camp lies in a wooded clearing in the area known as the Lonely Barrens.

I was unable to reason with the hard-headed chieftain, Kyleena Moonglow. Subsequently, I was forced to slay her and her entire war party. After doing so, I unstopped the streams, so the local farmers might once again have water for their crops.

I've convinced Kyleena Moonglow to move on and leave the local farmers in peace. She has agreed to unstop the streams and will order her people to retreat into the Misty Forest. I should return to Daggerford and tell Captain Frederick the good news.
Captain Frederick was pleased to hear I'd resolved the problem with Kyleena and her wayward tribe of wild elves.
Border Dispute

According to Baron Bugo, Lady Bronwyn, the sister of the late Duke Greatshout, has been missing for several months. While all of Daggerford mourned for her brother, Lady Bronwyn did not attend her brother's funeral rites. Recently, the Baron received unfortunate news: Lady Bronwyn has been captured by a group of extortionists who are demanding a ransom payment. Bugo has asked me to deliver a letter to Lady Bronwyn's kidnappers, who are lurking in the dark sewers near the Sorceller's Encapsulate.

Following Baron Bugo's precise instructions, I met with a group of skilled assassins lurking in the dank sewers beneath Daggerford. Unfortunately, these thugs seemed more interested in killing me than in reading Bugo's precious letter. After searching the sewers thoroughly, I found no sign of Lady Bronwyn.

After dealing with a gang of Xanathar assassins in Daggerford's sewers, Baron Bugo greeted me with a curious mixture of surprise and pleasure. After thanking me for delivering his letter, Bugo assured me that he would continue to investigate Lady Bronwyn's mysterious disappearance.
Bugo's Special Delivery

With the bandits beaten off, Teygan has revealed the second thrust of the Zhentarim plan. It seems that the Zhents are bringing all manner of goods, weapons, and troops into Daggerford, in caravans flying the colors of the Iron Throne. Teygan has learned, through his network of spies and informers, that one particular caravan of interest will be bringing important documents from the Zhentarim commanders into Daggerford. The caravan is currently situated in the forest, on the outskirts of Gillian's Hill. I am to prevent these documents from reaching Daggerford by whatever means, and bring them instead to Teygan.
I have recovered the Zhentarim documents and should bring them to Teygan as soon as I can. First, though, I should maybe see what Astriel has to say about all this...

Things are coming to a head it seems. Once Teygan had analyzed the Zhentarim documents, he was able to confirm the location of a Zhentarim base in Illefarn. I should talk to Astriel about this as soon as possible as I'm sure she will find it most interesting!

It also seems that a group of agents are on their way to Daggerford, for purposes unknown, but it doesn't seem likely that they will be beneficial. Indeed, they may be hunting me...
Caravans of Corruption

Hevesar is a man with plenty to worry about, and the farmlands around Daggerford are not a happy place to be at the moment.

To the south, shepherds graze their animals out in an area known as the Wild Pastures. These rolling grasslands are home to dangerous predators and are far from the relative safety of the villages and hamlets. However, the quality of the grazing makes it worthwhile to take the livestock there...until now. The number of animals being lost has increased alarmingly, sometimes from right under the noses of the shepherds themselves! I have agreed to investigate. Once the Daggerford town gates are reopened, I should travel to the village of Liam's Hold and meet Hevesar at the Holdfast Inn there.

Hevesar is a man with plenty to worry about, and the farmlands around Daggerford are not a happy place to be at the moment.

To the west of Liam's Hold, shepherds graze their animals out in an area known as the Wild Pastures. These rolling grasslands are home to dangerous predators and are far from the relative safety of the villages and hamlets. However, the quality of the grazing makes it worthwhile to take the livestock there...until now. The number of animals being lost has increased alarmingly, sometimes from right under the noses of the shepherds themselves! I have agreed to investigate.

I have met one of the shepherds in the Wild Pastures, a simple but honest man called Jerick. He mentioned the fact that limestone caves perforate the area below the pastures but did not think it likely that there could be something living there that has been stealing the livestock. It is clear that Jerick is wise in the ways of the wild, and his eyes are those of a man who has seen off many a danger, but I should probably investigate these caves nonetheless.
Entry004

Not long after arriving in the Wild Pastures, I witnessed a cow seemingly vanish into thin air, accompanied by a cackle of laughter! Someone or something is up to no good here, and it seems that they have magical help in their crime!

I have discovered a strange cavern system under the pastures and can hear the sounds of lowing animals and maybe worse, although it could just be my ears playing tricks on me. Regardless, I am sure that I will find an answer here.
Entry007

In a great central cavern, I battled a crazed goblin leader and a tanarukk with fire in its eyes and heart. All around us was the blood of butchered animals and stinking carcasses, the remains of the missing livestock.

On the corpse of the tanarukk, I discovered a menacing letter signed only "The Master." In my experience, anyone taking such a pompous name rarely has anything but trouble in mind. With the leaders killed and the goblins having fled, the shepherds' animals should be safe to graze these lands again. Surely this must have something to do with the problems mentioned by that farmhand in Daggerford. If I head over to Liam's Hold, perhaps I'll be able to pick up some reward.

In a great central cavern, I battled a crazed goblin leader and a tanarukk with fire in its eyes and heart. All around us was the blood of butchered animals and stinking carcasses, the remains of the missing livestock.

On the corpse of the tanarukk, I discovered a menacing letter signed only "The Master." In my experience, anyone taking such a pompous name rarely has anything but trouble in mind. With the leaders killed and the goblins having fled, the shepherds' animals should be safe to graze these lands again. I should report the good news to Hevesar.

Hevesar was very grateful when I informed him of my successful investigation of the missing animals. I faced considerable dangers in the caves beneath the Wild Pastures, but the plot to steal the livestock has been foiled.
Cattle Rustling around Daggerford

Yani Pavani, an interior decorator from Southern Amn, redecorated my stronghold. Yani promised to search for a custom magic item suited to my own unique tastes. I should check back with her to see if she has made any progress.
I hired Yani Pavani, an interior decorator from Southern Amn, to redecorate my stronghold. Yani even located a unique one-of-a-kind magic item and installed it inside my stronghold.
Decorator's Dilemma

It looks like I will be having plenty of time to get to know Astriel, as just moments after our arrival here in Daggerford, the town gates were ordered locked. No one is allowed in or out, without exception. This Astriel certainly has an inquisitive mind and has asked that I try to find out the reason for the lockdown. It does seem like a good idea to find out more, if only to know when it will be possible to leave.

The locking of the town gates was ordered by the Baron of Daggerford, one Matagar Bugo. I found this out from the rather insolent captain of the Griffons Mercenary Company in Daggerford, a man by the name of Dratharion. He did at least give me a reason for my unexpected detention here. Apparently a prisoner has escaped; a most dangerous customer called Wikkers. I probably have enough information for Astriel now and should see if she has been able to discover any more of what lies beneath Daggerford's seemingly peaceful surface.

I made my way back to the Chateau Elite Inn, and told Astriel everything that I had discovered. It seems she knows this Wikkers character, by reputation at least, and claims that he is an agent of the Iron Throne. Upon learning of his presence here, a curious look passed across Astriel's face, but I'm not sure what it meant. She seemed to find it quite amusing that he had let himself be captured.
Detained in Daggerford

I spoke with Korin Ironeater in the mines of Illefarn and learned that Duke Greatshout of Daggerford is alive! He and his sister are being kept as prisoners of the Zhentarim in the southeast part of the mines. I must find the duke and lady as soon as possible!
Entry002

I found Duke Greatshout and Lady Bronwyn in a torture chamber that the Zhentarim kept in the mines of Illefarn. The Duke told me of the Zhentarim plan to attack the town of Daggerford with an orcish force lead by an ancient devil known as Gorgomorz. They were then to feign a heroic rescue by the Griffon mercenaries, who are simply disguised Zhentarim. After saving the town and being hailed a hero, Matagar Bugo plans to solidify his rule and use Daggerford as a new base from which the Zhentarim can begin to infiltrate the region. The Duke has asked me to return to Daggerford in order to save the town from the assault, since the Griffons are now incapable of repelling the coming attack. The devil Gorgomorz could be defeated with an item called the Orb of Devil Containment, which Captain Dratharion kept with him.
Entry004

I found Duke Greatshout and Lady Bronwyn in a torture chamber that the Zhentarim kept in the mines of Illefarn. The Duke told me of the Zhentarim plan to attack the town of Daggerford with an orcish force lead by an ancient devil known as Gorgomorz. They were then to feign a heroic rescue by the Griffon mercenaries, who are simply disguised Zhentarim. After saving the town and being hailed a hero, Matagar Bugo plans to solidify his rule and use Daggerford as a new base from which the Zhentarim can begin to infiltrate the region. The Duke has asked me to return to Daggerford in order to save the town from the assault, since the Griffons are now incapable of repelling the coming attack. The devil Gorgomorz could be defeated with an item called the Orb of Devil Containment, which Captain Dratharion kept with him. After I showed the orb to Lady Bronwyn, she told me the secret words that will activate a portal from the mines back to Daggerford Castle. This portal is located near the torture chamber where she and her brother were kept.
Entry006
Entry007
Entry008
Entry009

I found Duke Greatshout and Lady Bronwyn in a torture chamber that the Zhentarim kept in the mines of Illefarn. The Duke told me of the Zhentarim plan to attack the town of Daggerford with an orcish force lead by an ancient devil known as Gorgomorz. They were then to feign a heroic rescue by the Griffon mercenaries, who are simply disguised Zhentarim. After saving the town and being hailed a hero, Matagar Bugo plans to solidify his rule and use Daggerford as a new base from which the Zhentarim can begin to infiltrate the region. The Duke has asked me to return to Daggerford in order to save the town from the assault, since the Griffons are now incapable of repelling the coming attack. The devil Gorgomorz could be defeated with an item called the Orb of Devil Containment, which Captain Dratharion kept with him. After I showed the orb to Lady Bronwyn, she told me the secret words that will activate a portal from the mines back to Daggerford Castle, and I was finally able to exit Illefarn. I must do my best to stop the coming attack!
Duke Greatshout Lives!

Last year, a young elven wizard named Deldarine apprenticed herself to the great wizard Edalseye in hopes of one day learning the magical art of planar travel. Time passed quickly for Deldarine; she was an intelligent and eager student, just as Edalseye was a warm and generous teacher. But one day Deldarine's peaceful world was shattered when Edalseye emerged from his planar gate a completely changed man. His soft blue eyes had turned to silver, and his usual warm kindness was replaced by spiteful wickedness. One night, after a heated confrontation with Edalseye, Deldarine fled the tower weeping, her face horribly disfigured by Edalseye's cruel lightning bolts. After arriving at my stronghold, Deldarine begged me to speak with her former master, the great wizard Edalseye, and to learn more about the strange ailment that afflicts him. Deldarine has promised to meet me in the Lonely Barrens outside Edalseye's tower.

Edalseye's tumbled stone tower is located on a remote island in the middle of the Lonely Barrens. Although she has suffered greatly at Edalseye's hands, Deldarine begged me not to harm her former master. Instead, I should learn the cause of Edalseye's strange magical affliction, and cure him if indeed he can be cured. Deldarine has opened a magic portal, which I can use to cross the raging river that surrounds Edalseye's foreboding tower.

By destroying the devil Abatorru's silver sphere, I have freed Edalseye from the evil devil's compulsive geas. But why was Edalseye transported to the depths of Baator? While speaking with Abatorru, I learned that Edalseye's faithful servant, Skully, might have been involved in this demonic game. Perhaps Skully holds the final clues, which will unravel this perplexing mystery.

After returning through Edalseye's planar gate, I discovered a strange imp attacking Skully. The imp, one of Abatorru's evil servants, must have secretly sabotaged Edalseye's planar gate, configuring it to transport Edalseye to Baator instead of to his intended destination in the Golden Hills. Although Deldarine lies dead outside the tower, I have solved the mystery of Edalseye's silver eyes.

Within the walls of Edalseye's tall stone tower, I have found a great library: an impressive room filled with dusty tomes, an odd arrangement of glowing magical pillars, and a foul-tempered pack of ice mephits. Both Deldarine and Skully have told me that I must ascend the tower to find Edalseye, but there are no obvious exits from this room. Great wizards have a famous fondness of subtle puzzles, so perhaps I should investigate this room very closely.

By melting the large ice crystal at the center of the library, I have released a foul-tempered water mephit who agreed to open a new teleportation portal. I should continue my search for Edalseye by exploring the tower's upper levels.

Edalseye's tower is truly a place of great wonders! Here in the exotic Chamber of Delights, dancing lights and colorful carpets clash in an unearthly scene, which only a plane-traveling wizard could love. Since there are no visible exits, I certainly face another one of Edalseye's twisted puzzles.

After solving a series of strange riddles posed by a loud-mouthed genie, I have opened a new teleportation portal that leads to the secret upper levels of Edalseye's tower. I should continue my quest to find the wizard Edalseye by searching the tower's upper levels.

After persevering through a complex series of challenging puzzles and infuriating riddles, I have finally reached Edalseye's cluttered bedroom, but the wizard himself remains elusive. Still, the strange assortment of magical artifacts in this untidy bedroom leads me to believe that the wizard is not far away. The ways of great wizards are subtle indeed, so I must search this room very carefully. Perhaps there is one last puzzle to solve?
Entry008

After learning that his former apprentice Deldarine summoned me to his tower, Edalseye lashed out in anger, calling down blazing lightning from the cloudy sky. Edalseye's lightning struck the ground where Deldarine was standing and she died screaming in an agony of blazing sparks. With so little humanity remaining behind those strange silver eyes, I wonder if Edalseye can be saved from his strange affliction. Still, after having come so far, I feel that I must reach the bottom of this curious mystery and thus will continue to pursue Edalseye.

I have followed the wizard Edalseye through his planar gate into the Nine Hells of Baator, where a powerful devil named Abatorru dwells in a world of flame and pain. The cruel devil, and his horde of vile servants, have enslaved Edalseye, twisting and corrupting his mind until very little humanity remains. Now that I have determined how Edalseye's mind was poisoned, I must find a way to save him.
Edalseye's Tower

I've met a mausoleum caretaker named Moris Olgrund who says the corpse of Elveronne Bricket is on the loose. He was extremely disappointed to hear that I would not help him track down the missing cadaver.

I've met a mausoleum caretaker named Moris Olgrund who says the corpse of Elveronne Bricket is on the loose. He says the man's sisters were present at the time of his demise, so I should travel to their estate in the farmlands west of Daggerford. Before I left, Moris handed me some holy water, which he suspects might come in handy.

The word "dysfunctional" does not adequately describe the relationship between Elveronne and his two sisters. Apparently, one sister dropped poison in the old chap's food while the other stole a prized necklace off the body before it was buried. I suppose I should question the two sisters further about this, though I fear to think where this might lead.
I recovered Elveronne's necklace, which seemed to placate him enough that he's returned to the crypt and shall trouble the living no more. I should report back to Moris with the good news.

I encountered the corpse of Old Man Bricket in the basement of the family estate. Before the cadaver could cause any further mischief, I banished its spirit back to the netherworld from whence it came. I should report back to Moris with the good news.

I encountered the corpse of Old Man Bricket in the basement of the family estate. Before the cadaver could cause any further mischief, I doused it with holy water, sending its spirit back to the netherworlds from whence it came. I should report back to Moris with the good news.

I always get choked up at family reunions. I'm sure the sisters were so happy to see their older brother...that is, until he snapped their necks like twigs. I should report back to Moris that I've managed to drum up some new business!

Oh, the delicious irony...to have slain the sisters with the same poison Muriel used to kill her brother. Now the Bricket family may be reunited at last. I should report back to Moris that I've managed to drum up some new business!
Moris was glad to hear that the situation regarding Elveronne Bricket's corpse had been resolved satisfactorily, and paid me handsomely for the services I had performed.
Moris was glad to hear that the situation regarding Elveronne Bricket's corpse had been resolved satisfactorily.
A Party to Wake the Dead

The Holdfast Inn has a fine reputation as a venue for supporting the arts, with merchants and patrons often making a beeline for the place to see some performer or other do their thing. The latest attraction is "Evani and her Incredible Fantabulizer®," and an audience from far and wide is expected for one of the most eagerly anticipated acts in years.

Sadly, they will be pretty disappointed unless there is a sudden change in the current situation. Evani's Fantabulizer® is broken and the owner suspects sabotage! Maybe I can help her to find the missing piece and do my bit for the artistic enrichment of the Sword Coast.

I found the missing piece of the Fantabulizer®. One of the local villagers had stolen it and was hiding out blind drunk in the wilderness. I should return the component to Evani and see what she has to say about this.

I found the missing piece of the Fantabulizer®. A villager called Lucas had stolen it and was hiding out blind drunk in the wilderness. He claims that the mage who has set up a tent on the outskirts of Liam's Hold put him up to it. It will no doubt be difficult to prove his story, as I am sure this mage won't readily incriminate himself if the story is indeed true. Regardless, I should get the component back to Evani and see what she has to say about all this.

The Fantabulizer® component is returned and Evani was extremely grateful. Before taking her leave to start with her repairs, she presented me with a fine magical ring that she herself had invented some time ago. With the missing piece safely returned, it shouldn't be too long until the show can go on! I do still question the motivations of the thief, though. Maybe I should drop by and let Mayor Wilsey know everything that has happened.

Mayor Wilsey's secretary, Miss Twinkin, spotted the visiting mage from the tent knock out Lucas! It seems that Lucas' story checks out and that this mage, Vejoni, is the instigator of all the trouble here.

It turns out that the "real" Vejoni had been consumed by some horrible creature that then took on his form! When I confronted the creature, it revealed its true form and attacked me, along with some strange constructs. It was a difficult battle but I was victorious in the end. Who knows what reasons the creature had for stealing the component and potentially discrediting Evani. Evani may have some thoughts on this, but it seems that what looked to be a simple case of trickery at the start, has finally come to a dramatic end.
Evani's Incredible Fantabulizer®

On Daggerford's docks, I met a troubled man named Fernigold the Elder. After some questioning, he revealed that his only son is missing. The father described his son as an avid treasure hunter who recently obtained an ancient map depicting the location of King Telarthir's forgotten tomb. Perhaps one of young Fernigold's friends, such as the dockside troublemaker named Klevtor, might know something of the young Fernigold's mysterious disappearance?

Fernigold the Elder's young son, the avid treasure hunter, is missing. His father, a poor fisherman living in Daggerford, has begged me to investigate. I obtained a copy of the last treasure map acquired by the eager young Fernigold. The map shows the location of King Telarthir's forgotten tomb, but what will I find in that dark place?

I gathered the broken body of young Fernigold from the dark hillside crypt, and carried the corpse to Daggerford. There, on the docks, I informed a distraught father that his only son had died pursuing his dreams. With tears in his eyes, Fernigold the Elder assured me that his son's body would have a proper burial and that his son's memory would never be forgotten.

Far beyond the encircling walls of Daggerford, in a small hillside tomb, I discovered the corpse of Fernigold's young son. The unfortunate lad died alone in the dark tomb, his face contorted by terror. I should bring word of this unfortunate discovery to Fernigold the Elder, a poor fisherman living near Daggerford's docks.

After finding the broken body of young Fernigold in a dark hillside crypt, I returned to Daggerford. There, on the docks, I informed a distraught father that his only son had died pursuing the lost treasures of King Telarthir.
Fernigold the Younger

Having returned from Illefarn via the Zhentarim portal, I was met by Captain Frederick and Astriel at the castle gates. They informed me that the majority of the orc forces had been defeated but a few remain at large. As long as these orcs elude capture, the town is vulnerable, and I must join in the hunt for them. With the militia conducting house to house searches I should probably look elsewhere...

I found the remaining orcs hiding out in the Daggerford sewers. One of them carried a note indicating that the attack on Daggerford is due this very night! I should get this vital information to Captain Frederick as soon as possible.

I reported the discovery of the orcs, as well as the imminent attack, to Captain Frederick. There is little to do now but to sit and wait. Having met Gorgomorz face-to-face, I do not relish the night ahead. And yet Astriel remains her usual cheerful self. She seems completely unfazed by the upcoming battle and I find myself drawing strength from that.
Find the Orc Infiltrators

My journey seems to be heading irrevocably towards the fabled dwarven deep of Illefarn. Illefarn has been long forgotten by most of the surface races, and therefore my problem is that no one actually knows where it is! Having spoken to Astriel, she suggested that I talk to Captain Frederick of the Daggerford militia. In her opinion, he is both trustworthy and likely to know where I might seek the location of Illefarn.
Entry002

Captain Frederick did not know the location of Illefarn, but instead suggested that I speak with Derval Ironeater about it. The blacksmith's shop, Derval's Bright Blade, is just across town from the barracks.
Entry004

I have spoken to Derval Ironeater and told him about the threat that faces Daggerford and the role of Illefarn in the plans of the conspirators. Derval was less than happy to talk to an outsider about Illefarn's location, but the situation is not as simple as it appears. It seems that Derval's brother Korin shares the same longing for Illefarn that Veiti, Derval's daughter, does. Indeed, he not only shares it, but has also pursued it, and so far as is known, is currently in Illefarn along with the Zhentarim! With so many lives and loved ones involved, Derval agreed to reveal the location of Illefarn to me but ONLY on the condition that Veiti accompany me on the expedition.

Once I am ready to leave, Veiti will meet me at the Daggerford docks where another dwarf, Magdaren, will transport us on her skiff up the River Delimbiyr, to an entrance into this ancient realm.
Entry006
Entry007
Entry008
Entry009
Magdaren has transported us to a place known as Laughing Hollow. An entrance into the ancient dwarven realm of Illefarn should be found here, somewhere atop the cliffs.
Finding Illefarn

I was approached by a small child who was distraught over the loss of her pet dog. It seems the animal fell down a large hole on a nearby island. Perhaps I should investigate, though I fear the child might not be pleased with what I uncover.
Entry002
Well, I found and slew that blasted imp who tricked me. I can now rest easy knowing the trickster's games are at an end.

It seems the child was actually an imp playing a rather elaborate trick on some unsuspecting do-gooder. Now I've been forced to do battle with an endless horde of hungry kocrachons. There must be a way to sever the connection to the kocrachons' home plane.
Entry004
I've managed to destroy the portal, which has eliminated the kocrachon threat. Now, I need to find that fiendish little imp who got me into this mess!
Entry006
Entry007
Entry008
Entry009

Well, I've managed to locate the imp, a somber and lonely little fellow named Boonmoppet. Apparently, the imp served as familiar to a powerful wizard who once lived in this tower. When the wizard passed away, Boonmoppet was left to his own devices. Without a new master to serve, the imp grew restless and resorted to performing elaborate pranks on the local farmers. He's promised to cease this disruptive behavior and will sell me magical items from his former master's supply.
Fishing with Live Bait

I've met a rather burly wainwright in Gillian's Hill, named Jouka, who had a valuable family heirloom stolen from him by a band of raiding lizardfolk. I've agreed to track down the item, which is a silver-plated awl. Jouka thinks the lizardfolk may have mistook it for a weapon and have probably taken it back to their home in the Lizard Marsh.
I found and returned Jouka's silver-plated awl. He was very pleased to have it back. Perhaps now he'll do a better job of keeping it out of the sight of raiding lizardfolk.
Jouka's Awl

Just as I was planning the color of my new carpets, Hevesar mentioned the inevitable complication involved in taking up residence in the abandoned temple outside of Liam's Hold. The mayor of the village wants to see a sign of good faith before welcoming such a well-armed neighbor with open arms. I am to go see her before she will hand over the key. The mayor's name is Wilsey, and her house is just south of the village market.

Mayor Wilsey is a no nonsense community leader, and I could tell that there was no way that she would just hand over the temple key. An infamous family of ne'er-do-wells and troublemakers, called the Munroes, has been causing a fuss in the village. Wilsey says that should I convince them to move on, it will be a sign that I am prepared to take on an active role in helping the community, and has promised to hand over the key once the task is complete.

I found the Munroes lurking along the Trade Way, just north of Liam's Hold, and it was a relatively simple matter to get them to leave the area. Once I report the good news to Mayor Wilsey, I should become the proud owner of one, slightly used, temple structure.

Well, it took a little bit of force, but I don't think the Munroes will be playing up around here again for a good while! Once I report the good news to Mayor Wilsey I should become the proud owner of one, slightly used, temple structure.

Wilsey was good to her word and willingly handed over the key to the temple. It should be interesting to see what I find in there! Whatever is to come, it is clear that I have made a good impression on the community of Liam's Hold and can expect a friendly welcome around the place.
Mayor Wilsey
Three pathetic-looking knight wannabes stand guard outside a foreboding cave entrance. They say the beast that lurks inside, named the Mighty Rat of Cunning Demeanor, slays all who enter its lair.

The MRCD's spokes-rat, a lively little rodent named Roo, is egging me on to challenge his master to mortal combat. If I accept the challenge, I should squeeze through a rock fissure on the north side of the cave.
This Roo is not only the MRCD's spokes-rat, but he's also its hive-mind! The "monster" is really just an assortment of highly aggressive rodents!
Roo raised "the white flag" after I'd made mincemeat out of his MRCD cohorts. I didn't bite, however, and slew the little so-and-so, as he so justly deserved!

Although it feels like I'm being rather lenient, what with Roo and friends feasting on the carcasses of scores of dead adventurers, I've decided to give Roo a second chance. The three knights-in-training will carry Roo back to Waterdeep, as proof of both their mighty strength and knightly benevolence.
I gave the three knights the skin of the dread MRCD, so they could take it back to their superiors and receive their promotion into the Order of Tye.
I gave the three knights the live MRCD in a sack, so they could take it back to their superiors and receive their promotion into the Order of Tye.
Mighty Rat of Cunning Demeanor

Ivus Barbarak has asked me to deliver the some ale to Rab Bitnez, who is having a party. I have to speak to Ivus' wife to pick up the ale. She's the queen of a small kingdom known as "The Holdfast Inn Kitchen," apparently.

I have faced many a dangerous creature in my time, but I'm not sure if I've ever faced one as dangerous as Nuli, Ivus Barbarak's wife. If her bite was as bad as her bark, then she would give an army of orcs a run for their money! Actually, I took the impression that underneath the fierce exterior, she has a heart of gold. She was grateful to me for picking up Rab's ale, which, by the way, is damned heavy. No wonder it has sat in the Holdfast Inn kitchen for a while.
Well, Rab Bitnez certainly has his ale now, although whether he is still in the mood for a party, I am not so certain. Still, it will keep for some time.
Party 6

While chatting up some locals in the Happy Cow Tavern, I met a curious halfling with a proposition that he says might interest me. He recommends I speak to the bard who is currently entertaining the tavern's patrons, and ask the man about a specific poem of his called "Peredus the Great."

I listened to Jorey Fontalas' rousing tale of the great hero, Peredus, who fought off highway bandits and fell down a cavernous well, never to be heard from again. I should speak with the halfling fellow in the Happy Cow about the significance of this tale.

Burnas Tellrot, an oddly-attired halfling in the Happy Cow Tavern, has asked me to meet him at the same well where the hero, Peredus, supposedly met his doom. Burnas believes Peredus' great sword may still lie at the bottom of the well, just waiting for some brave and talented adventurer to claim it. The well is to be found in the farmlands to the west of Daggerford.
I'm beginning to question the integrity of my adventuring partner, Burnas Tellrot. Instead of joining me in my expedition into Peredus' well, he chose to stay behind and leave me to my fate.

Apparently, the great hero, Peredus, did perish at the bottom of the well, as legends claim, but his restless spirit now wanders the cavern in endless torment. It seems the hero's bones have been defiled by a fearsome foe who lords over the gold and other keepsakes tossed into the wishing well. Peredus has asked that I reclaim his bones from the creature and drop them into a nearby magical stream, so his remains might be cleansed of the creature's evil taint.
The "creature" lording over Peredus' bones was a particularly temperamental young black dragon. After besting the creature in mortal combat, I reclaimed Peredus' bones.
Peredus was eternally grateful for having his spirit freed from the clutches of the evil black dragon. It seems the Tale of Peredus now has an ending worthy of its namesake.
Peredus the Great

Quite a story is developing out in the countryside around Daggerford! A young Harper called Teygan has apparently been looking to meet me and finally caught up with me outside my stronghold. Quite a charming young man he turned out to be too, maybe even too charming, and full of stories of Zhentarim plots in the region. Teygan has a base in the wilderness east of Liam's Hold, a region known as the Brush of Barbs, and I should look for him there for more information.
Teygan's base was easy to find using his directions. It should be interesting to hear what he and his fellows have discovered about the activities of the Zhentarim in the region.
A Rendezvous with Teygan
Captain Frederick seems as curious about the lockdown as I am. He asks that I seek out information from Captain Dratharion of the Griffons Mercenary Company, whose office is down the hall.

After meeting with Captain Dratharion of the Griffons mercenaries, I returned to tell Captain Frederick all I heard on the matter. From his reaction, I can tell he found the information quite intriguing.
I met with Captain Dratharion of the Griffons mercenaries, and received his take on the lockdown. I then tried to get some coin out of Captain Frederick before sharing the information.

Although I met with Captain Dratharion of the Griffons mercenaries, and received his take on the lockdown, I'm not sure I should share that information with Captain Frederick. Perhaps its best that he remains in the dark for now.
Play the Spy for Captain Frederick

While strolling through the stinking Lizard Marsh, I stepped right in the middle of something unpleasant: swamp politics. Redeye, self-proclaimed leader of all lizardfolk tribes, wants to crush the rebel tribe led by the upstart Saslick. Unfortunately, Saslick is allied with a powerful black dragon named Thuraskulusk. Attempting to break the alliance between Thuraskulusk and Saslick, Redeye has stolen Thuraskulusk's eggs and has asked me to hide the eggs inside Saslick's hut. Before approaching the village, Redeye suggested that I speak with the reclusive Green Hag who dwells in the Lizard Marsh. I should move quickly because Thuraskulusk is nearby, and she is hunting for her stolen eggs! I wonder what would happen if Thuraskulusk discovers her stolen eggs in my pack?

After striking a questionable deal with Redeye, self-proclaimed leader of all lizardfolk tribes, I secretly hid the black dragon Thuraskulusk's stolen eggs in Saslick's hut. When Thuraskulusk learned where her eggs were hidden, she confronted Saslick and incinerated him. After Thuraskulusk deals with the remnants of Saslick's rebel tribe, Redeye will once again control all lizardfolk tribes in the Lizard Marsh.

After striking a questionable deal with Redeye, self-proclaimed leader of all lizardfolk tribes, I have slain the black dragon Thuraskulusk. Now that Thuraskulusk is out of the way, Redeye's tribes can squash the rebel Saslick's tribe like tiny bugs. Soon, Redeye will once again control all lizardfolk tribes in the Lizard Marsh.

Redeye's Eggs

Vladmyr the Collector has asked me to locate three rare items that fell off the back of a caravan wagon bound for Waterdeep. He believes most of the items in the collection fell out of the wagon in the areas east of Gillian's Hill and Liam's Hold, and suggests I search there. The items in question include: a piece of elven sheet music, an Uthgardt burial totem, and a religious chalice brought north from the jungle lands of Chult.

I've managed to secure a portion of the artifacts that fell off the back of the caravan. However, I suspect Vladmyr will only be happy when I have all three in my possession. The items in question include: a piece of elven sheet music, an Uthgardt burial totem, and a religious chalice brought north from the jungle lands of Chult.

I've managed to secure all the items that fell off the back of the caravan: a piece of elven sheet music, an Uthgardt burial totem, and a religious chalice brought north from the jungle lands of Chult. I should take them back to Vladmyr at once, lest they be misplaced once again.

Vladmyr was grateful and amazed at my ability to secure all three of the rare artifacts. From his reaction, I imagine the combined worth of these items might pay for Vladmyr's retirement from the antiques business.
I decided I don't wish to work with Vladmyr the Loan Shark any more and declined his request to hunt down some missing artifacts.
I grew tired of dealing with Vladmyr and decided to put a permanent end to his extortions. I'm sure there will be a lot of relieved debtors in Daggerford tonight!
Scavenging the Countryside

Having uncovered the goblin cattle rustling operation in the Wild Pastures, I thought that the farmers' woes were over. But alas, this seems not to be the case. It appears that the shepherds have observed creatures moving about in the fields at night, and it seems likely that this activity ties in with some further unknown plan of the "Master." I am to head back to the Wild Pastures where the shepherd Gaslo will direct me to the spot where most of the sightings have occurred.
Entry002
Entry003
Entry004

I have met Gaslo (not the sharpest blade I have ever come across), who was able to describe to me (at some length...) the spot where most of the sightings have occurred. I need to camp down at the location of the skull of a giant beast that lies down by the river crossing the pastures.
Entry006

As predicted, I have ended up having to camp out under the stars in order to learn the truth of the shadows in the fields. The shadows turned out to be rather more solid upon close inspection; in fact, they turned out to be orcs! What groups of orcs are doing moving around so close to human settlements without burning and pillaging everything in sight is a very good question.

The answer appears to be that the burning and pillaging is planned for a later date, once the "Master" is ready. I continue to wonder who this "Master" is? No doubt, I will discover that soon enough. For now, I should once again report my success to Hevesar.
Entry008
Entry009

I'm definitely making a good impression on Hevesar. He was most pleased with my successful investigation of the orcs moving about in the fields at night, and we seem to have uncovered some more complex plan of this "Master." Something is brewing here in these quiet lands, I can feel it...
Shadows in the Fields

Although undead are not known for being polite and courteous to strangers, this Nosfiraat fellow seemed downright hospitable. In fact, I was so impressed by his courtly manners that I've agreed to destroy several ritual stones that ring the shipwreck with a magical barrier. Once the ritual stones are destroyed, Nosfiraat will be free to go and continue his duties as vampire-for-hire.

In keeping with the dishonest nature of his kind, the vampire Nosfiraat tried to parlay for his life with honeyed words and cunning schemes. In the end, as always happens with such grim, soulless entities, combat ensued and I slew both him and his vampire minions.
I had no inclination to listen to the honeyed words of the vampire Nosfiraat, and put an end to his existence before he could involve me in any of his cunning schemes.
Shipwreck Survivor

It seems that working with Teygan has annoyed the Zhentarim, and they have dispatched some of their agents with instructions to permanently halt my investigations. Teygan has discovered that they will be staying at the Holdfast Inn and has encouraged me to strike against them before they track me down.

I surprised the Zhentarim adventurers and was able to defeat them before they had time to prepare themselves. Such experienced and high-ranking Zhentarim are sure to have some interesting equipment with them that I will no doubt be able to use myself.

Teygan has deceived me greatly! A search of the Zhentarim adventurers' bodies revealed the fact that they all carry Harper pins! I have murdered in cold blood, and the only thing I have gained is the knowledge that Teygan is not who he claims to be.

Things are getting confusing around here. I ignored Teygan's warning to not engage the "Zhentarim" adventurers in conversation, and I am mighty relieved that I did. Drelia and her cohorts are not Zhentarim at all, but Harpers! The question now remains: who is Teygan? Drelia suggested that she accompany me to Teygan's base and I agreed with her idea.

Drelia suggested that she accompany me to Teygan's base but I told her to stay at the Holdfast Inn.

Teygan is Sememmon, one of the most evil geniuses in the world! He revealed his ruse to me and seemed to take great delight in his deception before teleporting me away back to Liam's Hold. He claimed to have received news regarding his missing consort, Ashemmi, and has now undoubtedly departed this part of the Sword Coast.

I went with Drelia to the cave but Teygan had already fled, leaving me a note. His true identity is Sememmon, one of the most evil Zhentarim geniuses in all of Faerûn! With Teygan's true identity revealed, Drelia and her companions have set off immediately, hoping to pick up on his trail and bring him some justice, Harper style. Everything has been turned on its head so swiftly that I have been left a little befuddled by all that has happened.

With Teygan revealed as Sememmon, I found myself increasingly annoyed by the Harper do-gooders and decided to kill them as Sememmon had originally instructed.
Showdown at the Holdfast Inn

Deep in the stinking mire of the Lizard Marsh, I discovered a hidden village populated by primitive lizardfolk. These disgusting reptiles capture travelers in the swamp and enslave them. One of the slaves, a half-elf named Igaleus, said that a fat lizard with a large wart on its green snout holds the key to the slave pen.
I used the slaver's key to release Igaleus and the rest of the lizardfolk's slaves. Before leaving, Igaleus promised to lead the slaves safely out of the deadly swamp.
Slaves to the Lizards

Astriel has been working the patrons of the Chateau Elite and one of them, a merchant, has revealed his annoyance at the strange cargos traveling down the River Delimbiyr. Cargo usually has to come into Daggerford and be inspected before a levy is paid. But this merchant has complained that barges are traveling down the river and loading the cargos directly onto sea going vessels at night -- a blatant flaunting of the regulations! Apparently, the poor fellow was getting quite vocal about things, and the doorman had to have a few quiet words in his ear, at which point he settled down to stew in silence.

The Mariners' Alliance seems the obvious place to start looking for information about what is going on here. It may be nothing, but Astriel seems to have a good sense for sniffing out trouble...

I managed to gain entry to the Mariners' Alliance basement, and have discovered that there is indeed something going on. The Shoreside Shipping Consortium is at the hub of whatever scheme is transpiring here. It owns both the barges and the sea vessel called the Barracuda, and if they do not have official sanction, then they have at least greased enough palms to ensure that heads turn away at the right moment. A visit to the Barracuda would no doubt shed more light on all this.

Onboard the Barracuda, I discovered that the ship itself is definitely being used for criminal activities. The captain's journal mentions shipments of weapons and armor being delivered to orcs, with payment in gold and slaves! Astriel is sure to want to know about this.

Strange Cargos

Talarenne, my great friend and companion, has been captured by some nefarious magic! I have no idea what kind of spell was used to take her, nor why she was taken, or even by whom. All I know is that she disappeared before my very eyes as bandits attacked our caravan, and that I will do everything in my power to find her!
Entry002

One of the other caravan passengers bears a likeness to Tala. I wonder if this could have been a case of mistaken identity then? This other passenger, Amara Leontyne she is called, seemed a little evasive on the subject...
Entry004

It turns out that Amara is actually a cover name for the Waterdhavian agent named Astriel.  Astriel believes that the caravan attackers probably did mean to take herself instead of Talarenne. She has said that she will help me find Talarenne if she can, so for now, I will just have to wait and see if she comes up with anything.
Entry006

I have found Talarenne trapped inside a magical globe of some sort! She was being traded between a foul tanarukk leader and Captain Herab, the cruel slaver of the Barracuda. Poor Tala! From inside her magical prison, Tala is able to speak with me, and she seems somehow sensitized to the magical Weave of our world. While I am obviously relieved to have my friend back, I fear for Tala's state of mind being trapped in such an alien place.
Entry008
Astriel has come good and claims to have found a way to free Tala from her prison! Of course, there is the "small" matter of defending Daggerford from an impending invasion first...
Tala is freed, and I have my wonderful friend back at my side! I do not need to write more, as words are insufficient to describe my happiness.
Talarenne

A key that I found while trawling the incredible assortment of junk and treasures in Torleth's shop has opened an ornate gate, which I discovered in a cave on the Crab's Claw Coast! Who knows how long it has been since anyone has passed this way? Through thick mists, I think I can see a building in the distance.

That's the thing with keys, isn't it? Each one has its use but a different lock is still a locked one... Having entered the stone building in the cave full of mist, the door immediately swung closed behind me and is now locked! I had better search for a way out of here. Merely being in this place sends a shiver down my spine and makes my hair stand on end. And yet...it is not altogether unpleasant.
Entry003

I have met a creature the likes of which I have never seen before. The creature doesn't seem to have any knowledge of who or where it is, how it came to be here, or any of the usual things you might expect upon meeting someone. Clearly, it is intelligent in some way, but a deep sense of tragedy radiates from it. Apparently the creature is a kind of ward against some form of shadows that have attacked this place, and I have agreed to help defeat these creatures once and for all. I must deactivate four mirrored globes and deal with whatever happens then... I find myself rather affected by this creature's sad story, and it is hard to think logically. This is such an emotional place!
Entry005

I have deactivated the four globes and battled a kind of shadow creature the likes of which I have never seen before! As I destroyed the final shadow, the creature at the center of the room collapsed, as if it had died. Surely I have not killed it? I have only known this creature such a short time and yet I could not bear its passing...
Entry007
Entry008

The creature Metastakixx is gone. To where I am not sure, but I fear to some oblivion. In the moments before its passing, Metastakixx seemed to find some kind of peace and wisdom that I do not really understand and maybe can never fully comprehend. I feel that I will never shake off the incredible intensity with which Metastakixx affected me, as if it was a being of pure tragic emotion. Indeed, so moved was I by the creature's passing, that I sung as I have never sung before; a song that seemed to come from deep within me and yet in some way moved through me without my consent. I feel truly blessed to have experienced this.

A Season in the Mists

Astriel's sense for trouble is once again sending me off on what might well be a wild goose chase. She wants me to spend some time at the Black Stone Inn, and as the name suggests, it's not the place for a quiet drink with some friends. Unless, that is, your friends are murdering scumbags with bad breath and a fondness for cheap ale. I don't know exactly what I am looking for, but Astriel has given me a rod of detection to help me find it. I won't look suspicious with that at all while I hang out at the bar!

Some wild goose chase! Astriel proved to be a very sharp operator once again, as I discovered Zhentarim activity in the sewers under the Black Stone Inn. Naturally, the Zhentarim were not exactly welcoming, but once I had prevented them from tearing me limb from limb, I found more evidence of weapons and orcs, and the rather worrying prospect of a deal with a devil!
Astriel was most impressed by what I had managed to discover at the Black Stone Inn, proving the existence of a Zhentarim plot in the area. I wonder what she will suggest next?
The Black Stone Inn

I have found my way to Laughing Hollow, a place that was once part of the Fallen Kingdom, an alliance of various tribes of elves and dwarves. The dwarves mined and worked in a vast underground complex known as Illefarn. Veiti tells me that the entrance to Illefarn lies at the top of the cliffs in Laughing Hollow.
Entry002

I have found my way inside the halls of Illefarn, a place that was once part of the Fallen Kingdom, an alliance of various tribes of elves and dwarves. The dwarves mined and worked in a vast underground complex here. Upon arriving inside the halls, the main entrance became sealed. Veiti's password no longer works, so some magic must be blocking us inside, likely the work of the Zhentarim. The only way to proceed now is deeper into Illefarn.
Entry004

Upon arriving inside the halls, the main entrance became sealed, and we discovered the bodies of many dwarves that were slain in a recent attack. After coming across a couple of Zhentarim guards throwing the dead bodies of the slain members of the Ironeater clan into a chasm, it would seem confirmed that all the dwarves are either dead or prisoners. This revelation undoubtedly weights heavily upon Veiti's mind. I must discover who is in charge of the Zhentarim operation in Illefarn and put a stop to them.
Entry006
Entry007
Entry008
Entry009

After descending deeper into the mines, I discovered Captain Dratharion in charge of the Zhentarim plot in Illefarn, and defeated him and his Griffon mercenaries. Veiti's dwarven wrath was at least somewhat appeased by this.
The Dwarves of Illefarn

Sejellus Krimp, the distributor in Gillian's Hill, told me that a group of thugs have taken up residence in the old tower southwest of his shop. Apparently, this tower was once occupied by Gillian Cantilar, the half-elven ranger from whom the town got its name.
I slew the infamous Gillian's Hill Gang, who were using Gillian's Tower to spy on merchant caravans along the Trade Way.
Sejellus was ecstatic to hear that the Gillian's Hill Gang would no longer trouble his caravans. He even paid me a fairly hefty reward, which was a welcome surprise.
The Gillian's Hill Gang

While traveling through farmlands east of Daggerford, I met a disgruntled dairy farmer named Porto Churlgo. Apparently, the young halfling sees dairy farming as an unrewarding venture and would like me to speak with his mother, Millie, about leading the family into a more profitable line of business.
I met Millie Churlgo, family matriarch and owner of Churlgo Cheese, who asked that I sample a bit of her latest product on the table behind her. A spot of cheese sounds good to me!
The relief in Millie's voice told me that slaying Yentai was the right thing to do. Perhaps now, the Churlgos can rest easy knowing that Yentai is six feet under.

The plot thickens, like a vat of day-old cheese. After giving me some background on the "real" Millie Churlgo, Yentai desires that I help him put the family out of business for good. I shall return to Millie and set the (cheese)wheels in motion...

I did as Yentai instructed and told Millie to evacuate her family to a barge tethered close to her farm. What happens next is anyone's guess. I only hope that Yentai is true to his word when I return to Gillian's Hill.
I tasted some Churlgo-brand cheese and was...underwhelmed. In fact, I don't think I've tasted cheese that wretched in my entire life. Yuck!

When I questioned Millie Churlgo about why her top-grade cheese wheels taste like low-grade cow patties, she explained that bandits have been wreaking havoc on her bottom-line, so she's had to drastically cut back on quality. I told her that I had little interest in assisting her and she appears somewhat 'cheesed off' with me now.

When I questioned Millie Churlgo about why her top-grade cheese wheels taste like low-grade cow patties, she explained that bandits have been wreaking havoc on her bottom-line, so she's had to drastically cut back on quality. She has asked me to accompany her son Porto on his next delivery to Gillian's Hill. Hopefully, we can get the caravan there in one piece.

I'm starting to get that itchy feeling like I'm treading in lands I don't belong. From Porto's constant bickering, to bandits attacking as if they were merely carrying out orders, the web of deceit around Churlgo Cheese seems to grow larger by the minute.

I'm not sure any amount of gold is worth the aggravation I've endured getting this shipment to Gillian's Hill. Even the trader, Sejellus, seems an ungrateful lout! Ah, the life of an adventurer can be trying at times...

Millie explained her family's long history with a devious Iron Throne crime boss named Yentai. Apparently, this fellow is demanding that the Churlgos hand over their valuable cheese recipes to him, or else! I told Millie I was unwilling to murder this Yentai in cold blood. She was none too pleased, to say the least.

Millie explained her family's long history with a devious Iron Throne crime boss named Yentai. Apparently, this fellow is demanding that the Churlgos hand over their valuable cheese recipes to him, or else! I've offered to get him off Millie's back for good, and so I must travel to Gillian's Hill at once. After I've slain this Yentai, I am to collect his amulet as proof of his demise.
It was my pleasure to slay the villain, Yentai. I should return his amulet to Millie so that she may finally be out from under his dark shadow.
The Great Cheese Caper

In a dimly lit cave on the outskirts of the stinking Lizard Marsh, dwells the Green Hag. She lives alone, except for a few rather sad-looking, warty toads. Never much of a "people-person," the old hag has been in a particularly foul mood after losing her precious hairbrush. To make matters worse, the old hag has recently begun to suffer from debilitating pains all over her wrinkled green skin. Fearing that these two unfortunate incidents are connected, she has concluded that her rival, a shriveled little lizardfolk shaman named Uzzak-Szalzik, has used the missing hairbrush to craft a magical effigy and is working some loathsome spells against her. The old hag has asked me to sneak into the lizardfolk village and find the magical effigy, her lost hairbrush, as well as a personal item from the shaman's hut, so that she can retaliate with her own spells. In order for me to enter the lizardfolk village undetected, the Green Hag has transformed my appearance into that of a lizardfolk. She has warned me that the transformation will quickly fade when I leave the swamp and that it does not disguise voices, so I must move quickly and avoid speaking.

Deep in the stinking mire of the Lizard Marsh, I raided a primitive lizardfolk village and recovered a strange magical effigy from their shriveled shaman, Uzzak-Szalzik. The Green Hag claims that Uzzak-Szalzik used this effigy to work dark magic against her, resulting in a rather uncomfortable looking skin condition. Although the hag cackled with delight when I gave her the effigy, it remains unclear if Uzzak-Szalzik was truly responsible for her rather gruesome skin. In return for my services, the old hag has agreed to sell me a wild assortment of foul-smelling potions and poultices.

Deep in the stinking mire of the Lizard Marsh, I raided a primitive lizardfolk village and recovered a strange magical effigy from their shriveled shaman, Uzzak-Szalzik. The Green Hag claims that Uzzak-Szalzik used this effigy to work dark magic against her, resulting in a rather uncomfortable looking skin condition. Although the hag cackled with delight when I gave her the effigy, it remains unclear if Uzzak-Szalzik was truly responsible for her rather gruesome skin. Despite my doubts, she snickered evilly when I pressed the Uzzak-Szalzik's bone knife into her wrinkled hands. With this stolen knife, the hag will craft an effigy and work devious magical spells against Uzzak-Szalzik. I am not certain what she is planning, but it might involve large quantities of boiling liquids. In return for my services, the old hag has agreed to sell me a wild assortment of foul-smelling potions and poultices.
The Green Hag

In front of the stone doors to the Hall of Wonder in Illefarn, I found six rotating stands that are used to support six reflecting mirrors. The ancient mirrors, however, have long been missing. It would seem that these mirrors could be used to reflect a beam of light, which may unlock the door. Veiti has said that five of them can be found in her uncle Korin's office, off the Feast Hall. Who knows where the sixth one resides, if indeed it isn't lost forever.
