I managed to find all six ancient mirrors and placed them upon their stands. Triggering the magical mechanism, a beam of light was reflected off each, eventually opening the locked doors. I wonder what lies within...
The Hall of Wonder

I met a curious character called Erik the Fin in the Daggerford Docks, who has asked me to find a chest that he dropped into the river Delimbiyr. He said it's most likely to be downriver somewhere, to the west of Daggerford, but he has been unable to find it. I have agreed to look for the chest, but there seems to be something that Erik is holding back from me. Perhaps I will find out more clues when I locate the chest.

I have found a strange chest within a cave in the Western Farmlands. There is a tiny voice coming from inside the sealed chest, asking that I take it to a mage called Delfen at the Sorceller's Encapsulate in Daggerford.

At the pleadings of the small voice coming from within the chest, I have delivered it to Delfen at the Sorceller's Encapsulate. Opening the magically sealed chest, Delfen discovered his missing imp familiar, Sujit, and both are happily reunited. It would appear, however, that Sujit's former evil master, Mogdor, attempted to have Erik the Fin kidnap the imp in the chest. In revenge for this deed, Delfen has planted a small "surprise" for Mogdor inside the chest and has asked that I deliver it to Erik. He has also advised that I do not accompany Erik after bringing him the chest, as it would put my life in danger.

At the pleadings of the small voice coming from within the chest, I have delivered it to Delfen at the Sorceller's Encapsulate. Opening the magically sealed chest, Delfen discovered his missing imp familiar, Sujit, and both are happily reunited. It would appear that Sujit's former evil master, Mogdor, attempted to have the imp kidnapped in the chest. Now that Sujit is safe with his master once again, my part in this little escapade is over, and I am free from having to lug a heavy chest around!

I have brought Delfen's "surprise" chest to Erik the Fin and he has rewarded me handsomely. I have decided to heed Delfen's warning and to not involve myself any further in this matter as it could seriously jeopardize my life. Delfen and Sujit are happily reunited and Mogdor will most assuredly get what he deserves...whatever that may be.
Entry014

I have brought Delfen's "surprise" chest to Erik the Fin and insisted that I accompany him to wherever he is taking it. I have decided not to heed Delfen's warning about what might happen should I be present when Mogdor opens the chest, but I just can't help but satisfy my curiosity! One thing is for sure - someone will not be pleased.
Entry016

The evil wizard Mogdor was annoyed at my presence but was gleeful at having the chest finally brought to him. He was greatly dismayed, however, to find not Sujit inside but a demilich instead! Erik the Fin fled in terror from the cave and a shocked Mogdor was incinerated by the infernal creature right before my eyes! Extallimix was its name, and it drew its unholy gaze upon me, preparing to unleash a deadly blow. Before it could, however, it became distracted by something powerful nearby and floated away, mumbling.

I have managed to find the chest within a cave in the Western Farmlands. It would seem that a bear pulled it from the river but was unable to open it, as it is magically sealed. There is a tiny voice coming from inside the sturdy chest, asking that I take it to a mage called Delfen at the Sorceller's Encapsulate in Daggerford. I now need to decide to whom I shall bring this chest: Delfen or Erik the Fin.
I met a curious character called Erik the Fin in the Daggerford Docks, who has expressed great interest in the return of the chest I found in a cave in the Western Farmlands.

I have returned the chest to Erik the Fin and he has rewarded me handsomely...perhaps too handsomely for such a worn-looking chest. The real value was obviously whoever was inside the chest that pleaded for my aid. Sadly, I shall never know who it was.
Entry006

I have returned the chest to Erik the Fin and have insisted that I accompany him to wherever he is taking it. Tiny voices emanating from sturdy locked chests are often signs that something disturbing is transpiring. I am going to find out what this is all about.
Entry008

It turns out that Erik the Fin was hired by an evil wizard named Mogdor to kidnap his former imp servant, Sujit, who had previously escaped him. Mogdor looked quite content to be reunited with his companion, although Sujit seemed far from pleased at the outcome and I swear it gave me the evil eye before disappearing through a portal with its former master.
Entry010
The Missing Chest

While traveling through the outlying Wild Pastures, I met a young shepherd girl named Lavna. After our conversation was interrupted by the howl of wolves in the woods, Lavna insisted that Old One-Eye, a fearsome worg of tremendous proportions, was responsible for the vanishing livestock. Lavna asked me to search the south woods for Old One-Eye and cut off its head.

After killing the worg known as Old One-Eye and returning its head to Lavna, the young shepherd girl reluctantly admitted that the worg was only responsible for the deaths of a few old cows. Still, Lavna was grateful to finally be rid of Old One-Eye.
The One-Eyed Worg

Rab Bitnez claims to have been attacked by something that flew through his window. Perhaps I should ask around town and see if anyone else has seen anything? Whatever is the truth of the matter, it is clear that Rab has been quite shocked by something; almost as shocked as I was by the incredible reek of garlic that permeates his house!

I spoke to Ivus Barbarak about Rab and the strange state that I found him in. As a publican, I guess Ivus has seen quite a few strange states in his time. He said that I should probably mention this to Mayor Wilsey, just to be sure.

The crypt in the cliffs is inhabited, and the phantom of Liam's Hold is revealed! A dark elf vampire going by the name of Sieronius Dethick is the culprit, and he explained to me that he is bound to remain within the walls of Liam's Hold until freed by his wife, for only she can break the curse that holds him here. Of course, Dethick's wife has been dead for centuries, so he plots to obtain for himself a new one. At the moment that I entered, he was waiting for Xanda to awaken from whatever sleep she is in, in order to complete his marriage ceremony and be free. Sensing the opportunity for some mischief, I suggested that he might like to meet Lula, the vampire wannabe from Daggerford. Dethick agreed.

I need to go and find Lula and see if I can convince her to accompany me back to Dethick's lair.

The crypt in the cliffs is inhabited, and the phantom of Liam's Hold is revealed! A dark elf vampire going by the name of Sieronius Dethick is the culprit.

Lying at the vampire's feet was draped the unconscious Xanda, and before he could complete his evil plan, we fought. The presence of the ink on this page gives the truth to my victory over the foul, lifeless beast.

Sieronius Dethick and Lula Redcap's marriage was a touching ceremony, although the moment when Lula's soul was wrenched from her body was somewhat more violent than the average punch up between the bride's father and best man! It is done. Dethick is free, and I am the proud possessor of an ancient item of considerable power.

The crypt in the cliffs is inhabited, and the phantom of Liam's Hold is revealed! A dark elf vampire going by the name of Sieronius Dethick is the culprit. Lying at the vampire's feet was draped the unconscious Xanda, and it was clear that I was too late to rescue her from his clutches. At least the village will now be free of his threat, as the presence of Xanda was the cure to the curse that has bound him here since ages past.
Entry015
Entry003

I spoke to Mayor Wilsey about Rab, and she assured me that Rab is on the whole a trustworthy fellow, unlikely to seek attention or become easily flustered. After a few moments, the mayor suggested that I go and talk with Nell the Baker's daughter, Jemmy, who has been having most unusual dreams, just to be sure that the two episodes aren't related. Nell and Jemmy live in the cake shop to the north of the village.
Entry005

I had a very interesting chat with the most unusual Jemmy Kirschtorte. Not only does young Jemmy apparently have a bat familiar going by the name of Mr. Barnabus, but it's also been instrumental in helping to protect mother and daughter from the nocturnal visitations of a "dream man!" The more I follow up on Rab's tale, the weirder things seem to be getting...
Entry007

Hegrad, from the night watch, was in discussion with Mayor Wilsey when I entered her office. Apparently, he was on patrol last night with Xanda when they saw a figure skulking in the shadows at the base of the eastern cliffs somewhere between the Holdfast Inn and Rab's house. They gave chase and Hegrad saw the figure disappear in a cloud of smoke, seemingly vanishing into the rock itself! When they later discussed it, Xanda did not seem to remember anything suspicious at all, and Hegrad put it down to the strange tricks that the night can play on you. This morning, however, he headed over to Xanda's house found that and she has vanished!

I should follow this up, and I am sure to find a clue either at the base of the cliffs or in Xanda's house.

I found Xanda's diary, and the last entry mentions a strange compulsion to return to the cliffs. It seems that she headed there immediately after writing the entry, not even stopping to eat her breakfast.
An illusion covered an entrance to a strange, crypt-like space in the cliffs! I am sure that I am getting close to the heart of this mystery now.
The Phantom of Liam's Hold

On the rocky shores of the Blade Cliffs, a poor hedge knight named Sir Griswald lays siege to Castle Exeltis. The siege fares poorly and Sir Griswald cannot breach the castle's thick stone walls. Despite the overwhelming odds against his group of knights, Sir Griswald believes that I can help him take the castle from his hated enemy, Lord Feldran Exeltis.

Late one crisp winter night, a beautiful young woman, carrying little more than a chest filled with rare gems, arrived alone in Baldur's Gate. When questioned, the young woman simply identified herself as Princess Soliana of Fanloc, and announced her intentions to seek a husband. Despite her unusual story, many young knights sought to win the princess' hand in marriage. Her two favorite suitors were a noble young lordling named Feldran Exeltis and a poor hedge knight named Sir Griswald. What happened next remains unclear to me; however, Princess Soliana is with Lord Feldran inside Castle Exeltis while Sir Griswald lays siege to the castle, resolutely maintaining that Lord Feldran has imprisoned Soliana against her own wishes. Since Sir Griswald's forces have been unable to breach the castle, I have been asked to find a way to lower the castle's massive drawbridge.

By reuniting the two separated lovers, Sir Griswald and Princess Soliana, I have successfully ended the siege of Castle Exeltis. While Lord Feldran lies dead in his courtyard, the two young lovers happily walked away from the castle.

Castle Exeltis' pretentious gatekeeper has suggested that Sir Griswald might quit his siege after hearing the good Princess Soliana express her eternal love for the noble Lord Feldran. I have been asked to bring Sir Griswald, alone, to the castle gates tonight at midnight.

It was a trap! Griswald's loyal knights were all slain in their sleep while Sir Griswald and I waited in vain at the castle gates for Princess Soliana. Sir Griswald, despairing at the loss of his loyal knights, charged the castle gates and was ruthlessly cut down by a hail of arrows. Princess Soliana and Lord Feldran both remain locked inside Castle Exeltis while Griswald's corpse now rots outside.

At Castle Exeltis, I have grown suspicious of the gatekeeper's offer, and have decided not to bring Griswald to the castle gates at midnight. Still, Griswald's forces remain entrenched on the shores of the Blade Cliffs, and I must find a way to lower the castle's massive drawbridge.

At the base of the Blade Cliffs, I met an old fisherwoman named Olree. She has told me how to enter Castle Exeltis through a hidden maze of sea caves, which lead into the castle's basement sewage cistern. Princess Soliana and Lord Feldran remain locked inside the castle. I must speak with them both before I can puzzle out the truth behind this curious courtship.

Inside Castle Exeltis, I finally encountered the mysterious Lord Feldran. He proved to be nothing more than a pompous fool pretending to be a noble knight. As we dueled, he savagely hurled insults at me, before fleeing like a shameless coward. I must be wary, for he is certain to return with reinforcements. Now, I must find Princess Soliana and learn more about her curious courtship with Lord Feldran and Sir Griswald.

After confessing her love for Sir Griswald, Princess Soliana has entrusted me with her strange secret. She is not really a princess, nor is she even a woman. Rather, she is a falcon who was transformed into a young woman by a witch's magic spell. She has asked me to lower the castle drawbridge, so that Sir Griswald might rescue her from Lord Feldran.

I have lowered the castle's massive drawbridge, and Sir Griswald's loyal knights have stormed into the inner courtyard. With a single blow from his great sword, Sir Griswald himself took the life of his mortal enemy, Lord Feldran. He then rushed into the castle, desperately calling out the name of his true love, Princess Soliana.

After confessing her love for Sir Griswald, Princess Soliana has entrusted me with her strange secret. She is not really a princess, nor is she even a woman. Rather, she is a falcon who was transformed into a young woman by a witch's magic spell. Unfortunately, the beautiful young princess blamed herself for Sir Griswald's death. In the midst of her despair, Soliana transformed herself back into a falcon and flew away from Castle Exeltis, never to return.
The Princess of Fanloc

The cattle rustling may be over, and a war band of heavily armed orcs defeated, but things are going from bad to worse for the once untroubled farmers around Daggerford. Hevesar's nephew witnessed his father and many other shepherds being rounded up and captured by yet more orcs, no doubt operating under the instructions of this mysterious "Master". The boy also managed to observe the orcs moving west, towards the coastal areas. Hevesar suspects that the orcs must have another base of operations somewhere in the area, and that were I to find this, I would also find the missing shepherds. Obviously, I should start my search as soon as I can in case they are sold to slavers...or worse!

reserved for astriel clue
Entry004

I have found Jerick and the missing shepherds penned up like cattle in a cliff bottom cave used by smugglers on the Crab's Claw Coast. They are exhausted but most of them remain alive and relatively unhurt. Jerick informed me of the presence of some powerful orcish leaders in a deeper chamber of the caves. I should seek them out and see if I can learn the identity of this "Master" once and for all, while simultaneously finding a way to free the captured shepherds.
Entry006

I discovered two tanarukk leaders in conference with the captain of the smuggler's ship I saw outside the sea cave. They fought with incredible ferocity but I was able to defeat them.

After the fight, I scoured the area and discovered a crudely written note alluding to a "Master" and a hidden base where the weapons are being transported to. There is more to this than meets the eye. A key on the fallen leader's corpse will likely open the slave pen, and the shepherds should soon be returning to their families.
The key from the tanarukk leader was indeed the correct one for the slave pen, and the shepherds have been freed! I should tell Hevesar and his nephew the good news as soon as I can.
Entry009

I have solved the mystery of the disappearing shepherds. The Zhentarim were using a sea cave to drop off weapons and armors for the orcs, the very same shipments that I heard about while investigating the Mariners' Alliance records. Obviously, this conspiracy was to be conducted in secret, and any shepherds who wandered too close to the action were captured and enslaved. With the sea cave discovered, and the leaders killed, the area should be safe for the shepherds once again.
Abducted Shepherds

I found the Ghost Smith, the spirit of a long dead master dwarven smith, in a hidden forge in the Upper Halls of Illefarn. The ghost wishes that a sacred stone belonging to his god, Moradin, be found. The stone is surely in Illefarn somewhere.

I have found Moradin's Stone that the Ghost Smith wished to have returned to him. I should tell the ghost that I now have it in my possession.

The Ghost Smith was very pleased at having Moradin's Stone returned to him after so many centuries. As a reward, he has offered to aid me with his crafting skills before his spirit departs this place forever. I may put one item of my choice into his work chest, so that he may use his forge to improve it. I should choose wisely.
The Secret Forge of Illefarn

Rain, rain, rain...it gets everywhere. Seeping through the cracks in the wooden beams of the caravan wagon and even down the tops of my boots! It can only mean one thing: I'm back in the Sword Coast. My good friend, Talarenne, and I have been traveling south from Waterdeep for a few days now, and while the incessant rain hasn't dampened our spirits too much, our journey is frequently broken up by detours around flooded roads, uncrossable fords, and now a fallen tree across our path. The portly merchant, Falias, has just woken me to inform me of this latest delay, and as soon as I've finished writing this journal entry, I will go see what Talarenne has to say for herself.

What was supposed to have been just a fallen tree has turned out to be a bandit ambush! Worse than that though, Talarenne has been taken by some devious magic, the likes of which I have never seen. This stretch of the Trade Way was not meant to be unsafe, and I fear for Talarenne. After all we have been through together, I miss her more than words can say.
The Story So Far...

Astriel is suspicious about the circumstances surrounding Duke Greatshout's death, and I agree with her. The duke was supposed to have been a capable warrior, and the story of him being slain by a wild boar does seem rather unlikely. It is possible that he was caught off-guard but it would have been an extraordinary stroke of bad luck. I should visit the local taverns and attempt to track down some of the others who took part in the hunt to see if any of them are willing to speak.

The circumstances surrounding the duke's death are sounding increasingly suspicious. Not only did the wild boar attack during a brief moment when the duke was separated from the rest of the hunting party, but his spear was found lying by the body, with the tip broken off. Apparently, the spear looked to have been sabotaged, and there is even uncertainty about the body, which was so badly mauled that the only way to identify it was by the ducal signet ring on the finger. Astriel is sure to be interested in this, but I doubt she will be surprised.

I have told Astriel what I discovered about the highly suspicious circumstances surrounding the duke's death. I was right; she wasn't surprised, and just greeted the news with a knowing look and a forlorn shake of her head.
The Suspicious Death of Duke Greatshout

While sampling some of Gildamesh's fares in the Black Stone Inn, he passed along a rumor about some sickly farmers to the south, who are dying in droves. He said I should speak with Liam Sunmist, the priest at the local temple to Lathander in Daggerford.

Liam Sunmist, who presides over Daggerford's temple to Lathander, has asked me to investigate what he believes to be an outbreak of vampirism in Gillian's Hill. He recommends that I seek out a local herbalist there, named Mabda, who may be able to provide some information to aid my investigation.

The eccentric Mabda believes this outbreak of vampirism marks the return of a long-dead (and now mythical) being known to the local farmers as "Gothma." This beast of legend is an enormous vampire bat that preys on the local livestock. If all the legends are true, the giant bat's throne room can be found deep within the bowels of the Gillian's Hill Cemetery. Farmer Callaway gave me a key that should permit me to enter the cemetery's underground catacombs. I must journey there at once!

It appears that this "Gothma" has little to do with the farmers' plight. A necromancer from the Dalelands, who was in search of more test subjects, apparently followed rumors of a plague outbreak to the small hamlet of Gillian's Hill. Once there, he set up shop in the local cemetery and began exhuming the graves of plague victims. With the help of a bat wing disguise, he was able to use the Gothma legend to his advantage. Since he didn't actually kill anyone, I felt it best to just convince this Daxiong fellow to leave the area and never return. I should return to Liam Sunmist, at the temple to Lathander in Daggerford, to relate the news of my discovery.

It appears that this "Gothma" has little to do with the farmers' plight. A necromancer from the Dalelands, who was in search of more test subjects, apparently followed rumors of a plague outbreak to the small hamlet of Gillian's Hill. Once there, he set up shop in the local cemetery and began exhuming the graves of plague victims. With the help of a bat wing disguise, he was able to use the Gothma legend to his advantage. Since this Daxiong fellow may actually have been the cause of the supposed "plague," I thought it best to slay him where he stood. I should return to Liam Sunmist, at the temple to Lathander in Daggerford, to relate the news of my discovery.

Liam Sunmist was quite surprised to hear of my news about a necromancer setting up shop in the Gillian's Hill Cemetery. However, he is pleased to know that the situation has been resolved. He has gifted me with a medallion that hereafter names me as Favored of Lathander.
The Truth about Vampires

It seems I have a talent for attracting those in need. No sooner had I stepped out from the Chateau Elite Inn, than one of the farmers from the lands around Daggerford approached me with an offer of employment, as well as a handsome reward. If I wish to learn more, I must seek out the appointed representative of these farmers, one Hevesar Dimpet. He's currently lodging at the charmingly named Happy Cow Tavern.
Well, I've found Hevesar Dimpet. Let's see what he has to say for himself.
There be Trouble Down on the Farm

Jared Deathstalker, a cleric of Kelemvor, has spoken with me about an ancient Netherese shrine devoted to Umgatlik, an evil undead creature. The shrine was recently unearthed by Savant Gumbril, a bumbling scholar from Waterdeep. Unfortunately, Gumbril believes that Umgatlik is a lost Netherese god, and relishes the scholarly fame that such an unusual discovery would bring. Jared has asked me to persuade Gumbril that Umgatlik is evil and must not be summoned. I must journey to the Crab's Claw Coast, where Jared will meet me near the shrine's hidden entrance.

Vetrixia Nightmaiden, a cleric of Velsharoon, has spoken with me about an ancient Netherese shrine devoted to Umgatlik, a powerful undead creature. The shrine was recently unearthed by Savant Gumbril, a bumbling scholar from Waterdeep. Vetrixia has promised that Umgatlik will reward me if I can persuade Gumbril to summon the creature. I must journey to the Crab's Claw Coast, where Vetrixia will meet me near the shrine's hidden entrance.

Along the cliffs of the Crab's Claw Coast, I have entered a hidden shrine devoted to Umgatlik. The shrine was recently unearthed by Savant Gumbril, a bumbling scholar from Waterdeep, who believes that Umgatlik is one of the lost Netherese gods. After seeing the ancient shrine for myself, I am more uncertain than ever about Umgatlik's true nature.

Vetrixia Nightmaiden, a cleric of Velsharoon, activated Umgatlik's ritual altar and was slain during the ritual. Amidst the subsequent battle with Umgatlik's twin succubi, the scholar Gumbril was pulled into Umgatlik's mystical portal. I wonder what he has discovered on the other side? I now have a difficult choice: travel through the portal or seal it once and for all.

After Vetrixia began the ancient ritual to summon Umgatlik, and was subsequently slain, I destroyed Umgatlik's ritual altar. Without the altar, Umgatlik's summoning ritual can never be completed, and I feel certain that I have prevented a great evil from wreaking havoc across the Sword Coast.

I defeated Umgatlik, an ancient, evil undead creature, in combat. Clearly, the scholar Gumbril was mistaken in believing that Umgatlik was one of the lost Netherese gods, a fact for which I am thankful. I'm sure that a bona fide deity would have brushed me aside without even a second thought.

By using the ancient ritual altar buried within the hidden shrine, I summoned Umgatlik, a powerful, evil undead creature, and released him to wreak havoc upon the Sword Coast. I'm having a rather good day!

Astriel has asked that I help her to investigate various suspicious and worrying events in Daggerford.

I shall seek out this Vlad the Loan Shark and see what I can do to remedy the boy's situation.

I am to enter the back room of Torleth's shop where I will find a portrait of a young Duke Pwyll Greatshout. I decided to let Davey and his father fend for themselves with Vladmyr. Maybe it'll teach the elder Halleran a lesson that he shouldn't go borrowing money from shifty loan sharks.

Teygan's base was easy to find with his directions, and once there he revealed to me everything that he and his group have discovered about the Zhentarim activities in Daggerford. Apparently, they are disguising themselves as bandits to raid non-Zhentarim caravans, like the one I was traveling with, with a view to gaining an economic stranglehold on trade within the town. Teygan has provided me with the location of their camp, and I am to find and destroy it as soon as I can. The camp is located somewhere within the Lonely Barrens, north of the Brush of Barbs, and will likely be well hidden amongst the trees there.

I have located and destroyed the camp that Zhentarim bandits have been using to harass the caravans using the Trade Way. I should inform Teygan of my success and I'm sure Astriel will also be interested to learn what I have discovered.

Any Zhentarim thinking of acting as would-be bandits will think twice about it now! From Teygan's information, I was able to easily track down and destroy the main camp, scoring our first victory! Unfortunately, it seems that this will just be a minor inconvenience to the Zhentarim, and there will need to be many more in the days ahead.
Bandits Beware!
